claims.text: The target component surface is prone to hot cracking and has relatively low hardness and wear/corrosion resistance.
Laser-activated surface alloying with a preplaced powder mixture can produce a diffusion-bonded, crack-resistant modified layer.
The laser-alloyed layer can improve hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance relative to traditional fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
Scanning a laser over a preplaced or fed powder mixture induces rapid surface melting, mixing, and resolidification.
The treatment produces a graded, diffusion-bonded surface layer with a refined microstructure.
The modified layer contains uniformly distributed hard precipitates, such as WC particles, embedded in a tough metallic matrix.
The graded precipitate-containing microstructure mitigates residual stresses and hot cracking.
Rapid laser melting and solidification enables in situ diffusion of alloying elements from the powder.
Rapid laser processing creates a metastable microstructure.
The laser-created microstructure enhances hardness and resistance to wear and corrosion.
Laser surface alloying reduces hot-cracking propensity relative to fusion welding.
The laser-alloyed surface will have approximately 20–30% greater hardness than traditional fusion-welded repairs.
The laser-alloyed surface will exhibit improved wear and corrosion resistance relative to untreated and fusion-welded surfaces.
The laser-alloyed surface will exhibit a lower incidence of hot cracking than untreated and conventionally fusion-welded surfaces.
The intervention is applicable to high-value, heat-sensitive components that cannot be replaced in whole.
Component geometry, available laser scan area, and thermal sensitivity may limit the intervention's effectiveness.
